comments.author: @Legacy_Inc.
comments.text:
There’s a simple answer: price per million token doesn’t say anything about how many tokens the model uses for a query. So you can have a cheap model, but if it uses twice as many tokens to achieve the same or better result as more expensive models, then the price per token becomes irrelevant. 

Another explanation could simply be that xAI have decided to eat the extra cost so they look cheaper and better to the public, but are in reality just artificially stat-boosted to look good in leaderboards and make a name for themselves so they stay in the AI race… That’s a valid business strategy by the way.
